# HLT-C2 eligibility proposal (A2, candidate)

Study: Woodall et al. (2018), Understanding the effectiveness and mechanisms of a social prescribing service: a mixed method analysis. BMC Health Services Research 18:604.

Proposal: eligible.

## Criterion 1: relationship in a public or publicly funded service
- The object is a social prescribing service attached to primary care in a city in Northern England. Wellbeing Coordinators support individuals referred by GPs, health, social care professionals or by self-referral (p.2-3).
- The relationship studied is the one between service user and Wellbeing Coordinator, and the links between primary care and the voluntary and community sector (p.8-10).
- "Provision of the service is free at the point of access" (p.3). The study was funded by Leeds South & East Clinical Commissioning Group (p.12, Funding), and the paper frames the service in NHS commissioning terms (p.1-2).
- Point to check: the text does not state explicitly who funds the service itself (as opposed to the evaluation). Free access, GP referral and CCG funding of the evaluation point to a publicly commissioned service.

## Criterion 2: at least one qualitative and one quantitative finding
- Quantitative: pre/post questionnaire (WEMWBS, EQ-5D, Campaign to End Loneliness tool, self-reported GP use), n = 342 complete wellbeing pairs, paired t-tests and effect sizes (p.3-7, Tables 2-6, Figs. 1-3).
- Qualitative: 26 semi-structured service-user interviews and one staff focus group (17 staff), thematic analysis (p.3-4); themes reported p.4-10.

Both criteria are met. Joint claims were not used as a criterion.
